From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — PulseMed

Alicia / David — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed next steps list so we can keep momentum.

Pain points & goals we heard:
- Data isolation / HIPAA compliance: you need dedicated GPU pools and customer-managed networking (VPC) for production PHI handling.
- Predictable latency for clinical features: target ~150ms 95th percentile for single-turn inference, spikes unacceptable for clinician workflows.
- Throughput: baseline ~50 req/s with peaks up to ~120 req/s during morning shifts.
- Cost predictability and contractual SLAs for uptime/latency.

Proposed Dedicated Capacity configuration (initial):
- Reserved cluster: 4x A10G-equivalent GPUs (reserved), warm pool to scale to 8 GPUs for peak.
- Autoscaling policy: scale at 70% CPU/GPU utilization and keep 1 warm replica per model shard to avoid cold-starts.
- Caching & batching: prefix/KV cache enabled for repeated prompts; latency SLO preserved with conservative batching windows.
- Security: private control plane, customer KMS integration (HSM optional), audit logs enabled for all inference requests.

SLA targets we discussed:
- Uptime SLA: 99.95%
- Latency SLO: 95th pctl under 150ms for the primary model path (we'll run load testing during the POC and set a contractual latency objective).

Next steps / asks from PulseMed:
1) Sign the attached PoC SOW so we can reserve the initial capacity and schedule engineering time. (attached: PulseMed_Proof_of_Concept_SOW.pdf)
2) Share an internal network diagram (or approve our suggested topology) so we can validate peering and firewall rules. (see: network_arch_diagram.png)
3) Security questionnaire: I'll loop in our security team; please share any vendor questionnaire items you need answered by next Tue.
4) Procurement contact / PO cadence so we can surface contract terms to our legal team.
5) Tech deep-dive / benchmarking session next week — propose Wed 10am PT for a 60-minute runbook + traffic profile review.

I'll follow up with a DocuSign SOW and a HubSpot deal record with the timeline. If the above matches your expectations, reply with confirmation and any minor edits.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Alicia — quick technical notes ahead of the benchmarking session:

- HSM/KMS: Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and we can configure HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest; will confirm the exact vendor integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM).
- Warm pools & cold starts: we'll keep 1 warm replica per model shard and use continuous batching to avoid cold-starts. For your 150ms 95th target, warm pool sizing matters more than raw GPU count.
- Model sizing estimate (initial): for your expected 50 req/s baseline and the model family we discussed, 4x A10G-equivalents should cover baseline. Expect to scale to 8 GPUs for peak with autoscale policies. We can provide a more granular cost / perf estimate after you send the traffic profile.
- Quantization: we recommend int8-aware quantization for the production model in the Dedicated pool to lower unit cost while preserving accuracy; we'll run evals in the PoC.

I'll bring a recommended resource plan and sample load script to Wed's session. Attached is a rough network topology (network_arch_diagram.png) illustrating VPC peering and private control plane endpoints.

Cheers,
